Here’s a sketch of how the ApplicationList page will look with the Edit button after Approved.

**Header and one sample row:**

```
┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────┐
│ Department            │ Application Type      │ Complete │ Approved │ Edit │
├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────┤
│ Acme Fire Dept       │ County                │    ☑     │    ☑     │ Edit │  ← link/button
│ (link to application)│ (readonly text)       │ (disabled)│ (disabled)│      │
└──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────┘
```

**In context of the full page:**

- **Title:** “FIRE PROTECTION FUND FY 20XX Applications”
- **Table:**
  - **Column 1 (Department):** Party name as a link (to GetSubmittedApplication or ApplicationProcess).
  - **Column 2 (Application Type):** Read-only text (e.g. Municipal, County Admin, County).
  - **Column 3 (Complete):** Disabled checkbox (checked if complete).
  - **Column 4 (Approved):** Disabled checkbox (checked if approved).
  - **Column 5 (Edit):** **Edit** as a button/link that goes to the Edit Address form for that row’s department (using that row’s `AddressId`).

So the user sees the same list as now, with an extra **Edit** column on the right; clicking **Edit** opens the existing Edit Address form for that department’s address.
